1.title: Don't Compare Yourself to Others
1.verse: A sound heart is life to the body But envy is rottenness to the bones
1.quote: The truest mark of being born with great qualities is being born without envy.
1.wisdom:
You would figure that the “competition, comparisons, measuring up, cliques, groups, etc.” would be gone once you leave high school and turn 18. You would think social pressures and people wondering about what everyone else thinks and does would go away.

It doesn’t.

I have seen far too many people well into adult life that are still comparing themselves to everyone else. They are still trying to keep up with the rich neighbor, thin relative, famous schoolmate, or popular fellow worker. It is a waste of time and not worth the effort. You can’t win, but you can lose.

High school, especially senior year, is rampant with people comparing where they are, where they are headed next year, and what they have accomplished. There is always someone who did better than we did and people whom did worse. The problem is that not everyone started in the same place and we know for a fact that high school is NOT the finish line.

We have each been given things we can control and things we can’t. You can’t control the fact that you are bright, smart, beautiful (your dad is allowed to say that!), and funny anymore than you can control the house, or even country you live in. You can control how you react to conflict, hardship, success, and commitment to God, family, friends and enemies.

Expect the best from yourself no matter what your circumstances. Don’t compare your success or failure to others. Measure your "place" to your own dreams/goals and what God wants for your life.

2.title: Seeking Advice from Others
2.verse: "Every word of God is flawless; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
2.quote: Successful people follow the same advice they prescribe for others.
2.wisdom:
They say in business that free advice isn’t worth anything. I disagree. Seeking advice to help you make decisions is critical to your success as an adult and a teenager. Finding people who have experience that you can use to make decisions about your life is really valuable. That advice can steer you in the right direction and help you to live the life you were meant to live. The formula I use is simple; you take in all advice and measure it three ways.

First, does it match up to the Bible? It is the one place I can trust. Then I pray about it. Why not get the answer straight from the top? What is cool is that even people who aren’t Christians or Jews live by the truth that is in the Bible. Most don’t even know they are following it.

Second, does this person giving advice have my best interest in mind? (Note: I first seek advice from people who are close to God. Whenever I am seeking real advice, I always see what their relationship is like with God at that time. Usually I will ask, “How is your walk these days? From there I can measure the advice.) Do they like me and care for me? People who love you are a great place to get input. Despite my shortcomings at times that is why you should always ask me for advice whether you use it or not.

Third, does this person have a personal interest in the question? If so, then I might have to be very careful with their advice. This is especially true in relationships. Seeking advice or listening to a boyfriend for example on whether to have sex with him before marriage would be a “bad” place to get advice.

Remember, I am your biggest fan and will ALWAYS give you an answer that is in your best interest, even if you don’t like it.

3.title: Forgiveness
3.verse: For if you forgive men when they sin against you, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
3.quote: The weak can never forgive. Forgiveness is the attribute of the strong. — Anger makes you smaller, while forgiveness forces you to grow beyond what you were.
3.wisdom:
There is probably no stronger attribute that a person can have than the ability to forgive and ask for forgiveness. In many instances it is just a very small action on your part and a huge impact on the people you love and even those you don't. The inability to forgive is much harder on you than it will ever be on the other person. The reason is that when you don't forgive, you give up control of your peace, joy, and, sometimes, sanity to either the other person or the action that occurred. That is too hard and way too much to give away.

The most challenging forgiveness for me is forgiving myself. How about you? I do really well when it comes to other people. It is almost easy for me to see the best in other people. When you see the best in others, their challenges, and their problems, then the things they do to you are much easier to forgive. It doesn't always work for me. The single hardest thing for me to do is to forgive myself. What is crazy is that Christ died on the cross so we can be forgiven. If we don't forgive others, including ourselves, then what He did was a waste of time. Even with all that knowledge and comfort, I still struggle with that area.

How are you at forgiving others? Are there things and people you need to forgive? What about yourself? Do you need to ask forgiveness? Are you clean there as well? I hope so. I love you too much to have you burdened when the ability to forgive and be forgiven is right there in front of you. Just to make sure you are reading these, if you say the word forgiveness and give me a high five, I will give you five dollars.

4.title: Men and their Mom's
4.verse: Honor your father and mother so that you will live a long time in the land that the Lord your God is going to give you.
4.quote: How sharper than a serpent’s tooth it is to have a thankless child!
4.wisdom:
Watch how the guys you date treat their mother. It is the best window you will have to how they will treat you. If they treat their mother kindly, then there is a higher probability they will also treat you well. Think back to when you were growing up. You can think of lots of examples of your friends and how they treated their moms. Most of my friends were pretty good at it. How were your friends?

You can learn a lot about a man in how he treats his mother. Is he kind to her? Does he make fun of her (mean not good natured fun...)? Does he speak kindly to her? Does he respect her? Does he lift her up in front of others? Does he honor her? There is a 100% chance; he will treat his future wife the exact same way he treats his mother.

Remember he took a lifetime to learn how to treat his mother. These are habits that will be copied in the future and not forgotten.

5.title: Character
5.verse: Give her credit for all she does. She deserves the respect of everyone.
5.quote: Be more concerned with your character than your reputation, because your character is what you really are; your reputation is merely what others think you are.
5.quote_attr: John Wooden - Hall of Fame Basketball Coach
5.wisdom:
It’s hard not to be a hypocrite. Everyone ends up being one occasionally. For the most part, we start acting like someone else or trying to be something we are not. We say one thing and do something else. We try to impress our friends, hide things from our parents, go along with the crowd, and even show off. Sometimes our bad behavior doesn’t look so bad when we are around people with worse behavior. Our odor, while awful, doesn’t “smell” so bad because those around us are much worse!

The secret to character—and the true measure of any hypocrite—is how you act when you are alone. You can tell who you truly are when you are by yourself and no one else can see you—when it is just God and you alone. How you act when you are by yourself speaks volumes about your character. Are you honest? Do you hold yourself accountable? Are you the same person alone as with other people? If someone were watching, would you be proud of your actions?

Be a person of character first when you are by yourself, and then when you are around other people and it will be much easier.

6.title: Treat you like a "Queen"
6.verse: Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself up for her.
6.quote: Whether they give or refuse, it delights women just the same to have been asked.
6.wisdom:
This is the first of a many part series on men/boys. Who better to give you advice than a male? Actually, who better to give you advice than your Dad? Here are the minimum requirements for both the guys you date and, ultimately, the man you marry someday.

Minimum requirement #1: Treat you like a "queen".

I cannot emphasize how important it is that you find someone who treats you wonderfully. You deserve to have someone treat you that way EVERY DAY. Not just sometimes or a relationship where “this boyfriend” wasn’t like that. All the time is the only answer. If you settle in even one small relationship, you will begin to think that it is okay to not be treated well.

Like a "queen" means you are precious, special, respected, cared for, protected when necessary, and most important owned by God and should be treated as such. It isn’t hard to recognize. You will know it when you see it.

The type of people you date are ultimately a reflection on you. If you date someone who is selfish, self-absorbed, and totally focused on themselves, it reflects that you don’t think much of yourself. Don’t choose people who don’t appreciate you. Does that make sense?

Be around men that lift you up, like you, and, of course, draw you closer to Christ.

7.title: The Perfect College Day
7.verse: There is an appointed time for everything. And there is a time for every event under heaven.
7.quote: Half our life is spent trying to find something to do with the time we have rushed through life trying to save.
7.quote_attr: Will Rogers (1879 - 1935) New York Times, April 29, 1930
7.wisdom:
There are 24 hours in a day. Here is what a successful college student figures out prior to going to school:

A PERFECT COLLEGE DAY

Sleep---8 hours School---3 hours Eating---3 hours Studying ---3 hours Everything else---7 hours Total---24 hours

If you can figure this out early enough, college will be a very successful experience. You are given 24 hours each day and if you can discipline yourself to get enough sleep, and make sure you study every day you will do amazingly well. Managing your time is huge in college. Seven hours is an enormous amount of time each day to have fun, work, hang out, etc. The change from high school is pretty alarming.

Your ability to be focused in an environment of freedom is a challenging adjustment. I made sure that I went to the library and studied there. Every time I tried to study in my dorm I would get distracted. We also had a dorm study hall area that worked as well.

Study every day and you will be surprised how well you do in every other part of college.

8.title: Words
8.verse: A soft answer turns away wrath but a harsh word stirs up anger
8.quote: The difference between the almost right word and the right word is really a large matter-ʻtis the difference between the lightning-bug and the lightning.
8.wisdom:
For some reason, the older you get the more important your words become. As a kid, you get a lot more leeway in what you say to people. Sometimes the fact that you are a teenager allows you to “get away” with comments that are passed off as being just something a teenager would say. When you are an adult those words aren’t as easily passed by and, more importantly, the responsibility for what you say and do changes. As an adult, you are responsible for not only your actions, but also your words. For instance a complaint, criticism, feeling, or even just an opinion holds more weight as an 18-year old than it does as a 17-year old.

I encourage you to begin now to measure your comments and thoughts when you speak, especially to those you love. Your words to your Mom can hurt. They can hurt me as well. Be aware of what you are saying and why. So many people hurt others or get hurt by unkind, flippant words that with just a little extra care and maturity could have been avoided.

9.title: Wow! You are Special
9.verse: That is my commandment that You love one another as I have loved you.
9.quote: To love is to receive a glimpse of heaven.
9.wisdom:
I am really proud of you. There is no other way to put it. You are really something special and you are far more than I ever could have imagined when you were born.

The joy you bring me is immeasurable. There are so many things about you that I really like. I am so blessed to have you as a daughter. I can’t wait to see what you will be like as you get older. I can’t wait to meet your husband some day and I sure can’t wait to see what your kids are going to be like. Can you really imagine what your kids are going to be like someday? Think about it!

This is supposed to be 52 things you need to know. This one is simple: I love you VERY VERY much!

10.title: Healthy Eating
10.verse: For do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you whom you have from God, and you are not your own.
10.quote: Outside of every fat man there was even a fatter man trying to close in.
10.wisdom:
“You are what you eat.” Kind of a corny saying, but it really is true. Sadly there are a ton of bad food choices available all day. It seems like the more stress and time constraints the worse we have a tendency to eat. Eating healthy is a great skill to learn in life. An understanding of nutrition and health will benefit you, your friends, and, ultimately, your future husband and family.

As you know, all this great information when used for good is great. Just remember that exercise, eating healthy, and getting plenty of sleep, all add up to a “healthy body” that you can use to pursue all your dreams and goals. Please forgive the analogy, but it is a lot like a car. If you put the right fuel in it, take care of the car and drive it the way the "manual" says it will perform great. If you only focus on the way it looks and not the engine, you will eventually run into trouble. With a car, you can get a new one. Our bodies are with us forever. There are many women; yes adult women as well (men for that matter too...) who struggle in this area. It is something you must watch out for and be aware.

On another note, many women start to see themselves in the mirror much differently than they actually are. This can lead to eating disorders. It causes great pain and they can struggle in this area each and every day. (Once you have an eating challenge, you have it for your whole life.)

Being healthy and seeing yourself as healthy go together. If you find yourself confused or questioning, ask someone that loves you and get their “healthy” opinion.

11.title: Money
11.verse: Whoever loves money will never have enough money Whoever loves wealth will not be satisfied with it. This is also useless
11.quote: Lack of money is no real obstacle; lack of an idea is an obstacle.
11.wisdom:
One of things that a man I worked for taught me made a difference. One day he said to me; “Why do you choose to be poor?” I didn’t have a really good answer so I told him that I didn’t choose to be poor. He said based on how hard I worked and what job I was doing, I was choosing to be poor.

That always seemed a little harsh. Not everyone works for money. Poor in money does not mean poor in spirit, poor in friends, or poor in anything else. How much you make will never matter if you have a healthy perspective of money. Obviously, money does exist, and there is something to learn from this statement.

What I have learned since then is that a lot of people, who are much dumber than I am, make a lot more money than I do. Conversely, there are hundreds of thousands of people, who are A LOT smarter than I am, that don’t make as much as I do. Making money is a choice. I always felt like it was a really effective way to keep score. It is not the only way to keep score, but it was one way to keep score. I also made a commitment that when I left a company, it was either going to be in a sea of red ink (losses) or black ink (profits), but never in handcuffs.

That is a pretty good business principle to live by.

12.title: What Men say...
12.verse: What is desired in a man is kindness, and a poor man is better than a liar
12.quote: Every one in a crowd has the power to throw dirt: nine out of ten have the inclination.
12.wisdom:
One of the biggest risks we take when we are connected to someone else is that we take what they say and it becomes fact. It is obvious that the person you marry or seriously consider marrying is going to find you attractive. First off, you are and there is no denying that, but second, it is important that they love you “anyway.”

It is very unhealthy to have a relationship based on physical attraction. It is especially unhealthy if your boyfriend or, worse, husband is consistently criticizing how you look. You don’t want to be connected to a guy that is telling you what is wrong with you physically. Over time it will negatively affect you no matter what your level of self-confidence is.

Stay away from the guys that tell you to lose a few pounds or dress nicer or change your make up.

13.title: Sometimes No Advice is Better
13.verse: I can do all things through Christ, who gives me strength.
13.quote: I know God will not give me anything I can't handle. I just wish that He didn't trust me so much.
13.wisdom:
When you are right in the middle of God’s will, you know it by the Bible, by prayer, and by those around you who are Godly and have wisdom. Stay there and keep your path.

Don’t listen to anyone else, including me.

14.title: Alcohol, Drugs & Tobacco
14.verse: Wine and beer make people loud and controlled It is not wise to get drunk on them.
14.quote: There are two things that will be believed of any man whatsoever, and one of them is that he has taken to drink.
14.wisdom:
Don’t drink and drive. I know it sounds simple, but don’t. Don’t ride with other people who are drinking. I did and it is by the sheer grace of God that I am alive. If just one time something had gone wrong, it would have wrecked my life and others. You will get the chance. The risk is too high.

Two more comments about alcohol, drugs, and cigarettes for you. Obviously, stay away from them. Hopefully, up to now you have. Beware that you really can’t know if you have an addictive behavior until it is too late. They say that some people become addicted quicker than others do. If you stay away, you never have the risk of being addicted.

Sometimes with alcohol or drugs you get addicted not to the substance, but to how you think you look when you are doing it. I remember kids thinking they were funnier or cooler when they did them. They weren’t. They just looked stoned or drunk. They were funny, but not a respectful funny. This is especially true of cigarettes. I have seen way too many smart people still smoking because they can’t stop. That is an area I always wanted to avoid, where some substance controls me.

My other comment is that you need to be very careful if you ever drink when you are around men. Let's be clear not every man is a risk. There is nothing more awful than a girl who is taken advantage of by a man when she is under the influence. Believe me there are men (even ones who seem nice) who will take advantage if they can. Don't put yourself in that position. If you are in control of your body and mind, everything will go much better.

15.title: The Only Measurement
15.verse: Wisdom begins with respect for the Lord Those who obey his orders have good understanding He should be praised forever.
15.quote: It ain't those parts of the Bible that I can't understand that bother me, it's the parts that I do understand.
15.wisdom:
Jesus Christ is the only answer when there are no answers, but also when there are answers. Don’t measure your decisions, actions, attitudes, career choices, or spousal selection against anything else but Him. If you remember that He is the model, you cannot go wrong. As soon as you depend on a human (including yourself), you will get let down sometime, somewhere. I am great example of that. I can parade past you ten people that will tell you how wonderful I am in comparison to others they know. You know, and I know, my past sins. While an example in some areas, I fall very, very short. For whatever it is worth, so does everyone else, even if you can’t see it.

You fall short too. Right now, you are blessed and you have the whole world in front of you. The need for Jesus may not seem as strong or necessary. Trust me. You need Him. He is the only real help you can count on for the rest of your life. Learn that while the sun is shining, rather than while it is raining.

Life was meant to be lived His way. There are other ways, but they are not as rewarding or as exciting.

16.title: Marry a Godly Man
16.verse: What I am telling you is good, So do not forget what I teach you.
16.quote: It is very difficult to live among people you love and hold back from offering them advice.
16.wisdom:
Purpose yourself to have all of the important men in your life someday be my friend. I know today you may roll your eyes, but it will be one of the very best moves you can ever make. Up to now you have pretty much avoided me in most of your friendships. You may do that for a while longer, but don’t do it forever. The more I know about them the better it will be for you and for him.

I will say it anyway. Marry a Godly man. This requires you to date Godly men first. If you don’t start right you won’t finish right. This means that you ask them if they are Christians. You seem to have done a good job on this so far from what I can tell and the people you have let me see. I know that not all Christian boys are perfect. There may be kids I have seen or met that have totally fooled me, and are the worst behaving and acting people around. We don’t lack hypocrites in this world in any area. Don’t let one or two, or ten, bad examples dispel the fact that you want to keep looking for Christian men to have in your life. To get there ask two simple questions:

1. What is your story on how you met Christ? You know the right answer. It isn’t “I go to church, I was baptized as a child, I’m a Methodist/Catholic/ Baptist, etc.”

2. Tell me where you worship today. You know the right answer here as well. You are looking for someone who is bearing fruit, active in their church, etc. (Note: Another great sign is if they ask you the same questions!)

I know you want to marry someone you can respect and admire. Make sure he is Godly. When you do that, you will know that he is relying on someone other than himself. Just because he is successful doesn’t mean he will treat you and your kids well. I do know that if he loves the Lord there is no guarantee either. However, if he loves the Lord then there is always hope that if he does stray from the Lord; he will come back. That is something you can count on. If you both rely on God there will be no questions that don’t have an answer and no problem that can’t be solved. It requires both of you to have a common belief and a common hope.

17.title: Money is a Tool
17.verse: The more wealth people have The more friends they have to help spend it. So what do people really gain? They gain nothing except to look at their riches.
17.quote: A wise man should have money in his head; not in his heart.
17.wisdom:
Money is a tool. You work to live, not live to work. Any other concept regarding money will only cause pain and heartache someday. Money does not make you better or worse. It does not buy happiness; it can only buy you a feeling of financial security. Knowing you are not going to the poor house is nice, but it won’t fulfill your life.

Be open with your money. Give it to God, your family, friends and people and causes in need. Do it in that order. If you grip it too tight you will lose it or worse, spend your entire life trying not to lose it. Money is not important. It is serious, but it is not important.

18.title: I Love you Anyway
18.verse: Love patiently accepts all things. It always trusts, Always hopes, and always remains strong.
18.quote: Love and a cough cannot be hid.
18.wisdom:
I love you. They are the most powerful words on earth. For many people they are like oxygen. Love is a choice not a feeling. It is an action we take to “love someone” right where they are.

I saw a skit at Fellowship Church. They said:

**Wrong:** I love you BECAUSE...you love me, you behave, you are smart, pretty, and you don’t talk back with me.

**Wrong:** I love you IF… you love me, you get good grades, you agree with me, you don’t get fat, etc.

**Right:** I love you ANYWAY. No matter what. There is nothing you can make me do to stop loving you.

Make sure that when you love; you choose to love ANYWAY. Otherwise, it is really complicated and awfully disappointing for those you love and those that love you.

Make sure you tell people, all the time. It makes a big difference. It doesn’t matter if you are mad or angry. You can still love people that you are mad or angry with; it just may be a little bit harder.

19.title: Crying
19.verse: His anger lasts only a moment But His kindness lasts for a lifetime Crying may last a night But joy comes in the morning.
19.quote: Those who do not feel pain; seldom think it is felt
19.wisdom:
I boo-hoo pretty easily at sad movies and I can be a faucet more often at happy and joyful moments. I am going to cry when you get married and God-willing when you have a kid. Guys have a tendency to try and hide it. We are idiots. Why all the crying talk? I guess I just want you to hear from a “guy” how healthy it is too feel so strongly about things and events in your life (good or bad) that it makes you want to cry.

I have seen you cry lots of times. You are actually beautiful when you cry! Don’t try and stop the water works anywhere in life (except maybe at work. If it is possible-and it isn’t always possible- this would be the only place, I wouldn’t cry). Keep on crying for joy! It is also important that you grieve when there is loss. Not forever, so it controls your life, but grieve. With Christ’s strength you will get through it. Experience all that God has for you in every type of emotion.

For “cryin-out-loud”…keep the tears flowing.

20.title: "Old" Friends
20.verse: A faithful friend is the medicine of life
20.quote: In prosperity our friends know us; in adversity we know our friends.
20.wisdom:
Friends are huge in your life. They can have a dramatic impact on who you are and what you do. You have heard all of the recommendations you want about “If you hang around with trash…you will start to smell like it,” etc.

I am really partial to my early childhood friends because I have known them for so long. I don’t really have a lot in common (different states, jobs, hobbies etc.) with most of them other than my childhood. I really like that connection. Most of the time when we get together it is to talk about old times. To laugh and joke about the dumb things we did, said, or thought. I really, really like those memories and I love talking with them.

Stay close to all of your former friends if you can, even if you rarely get to see them. Sometimes it is just fun to get together and talk about how you “used to be friends.” You don’t have to replace them; they just become old friends that for the most part you talk about “old things.”

Some twenty years from now maybe you will be in touch with some of your old friends or maybe you won’t. When you do see them, you can still have fun and for that time, you can still be close friends.

21.title: Leadership
21.verse: Depend on the Lord in whatever you do And your plans will succeed
21.quote: The final test of a leader is that he leaves behind him in others the conviction and will to carry on.
21.wisdom:
It is hard to teach people to “give it their best.” This is especially true in school. Some people don’t really try and are bitter about the outcomes and choices they get for college and jobs even though they know deep in their heart that they didn’t really try hard enough. I am sure you have friends that are bummed about their ability to get into the college of their choice yet they never worked very hard. Your effort counts. Your drive to be successful in school can and will pay off.

What do you do with this “drive” that you have? How can you use it in other areas besides school? You know how to work hard and you know that when you do great things happen. Can you apply it to your relationships? Can you apply it to the areas that you serve? Can you apply it to teaching others the things they need to learn that you already have mastered? Can you individually change the world? Can you make a difference for Jesus on this earth? Can you influence a generation, country, town, family or just one person?

The answer is yes...

22.title: Lying
22.verse: If you respect the Lord, you will also hate evil I hate pride, bragging, evil ways and lies
22.quote: A liar needs a good memory.
22.wisdom:
You have probably read a zillion messages on this subject. Just some simple thoughts:

Tell the truth because it is the easiest thing to remember.

One of my favorite lines from a movie is “You can’t handle the truth.” Some people can’t. If it doesn’t edify or correct in love; it is not necessary to always tell somebody something even if it is the “truth.” That is not lying. It is being kind. (Example of someone saying: You are fat and you need to lose weight!”)

Don’t lie to yourself. This one will do the most damage. The 12 step programs for drinking, drugs, etc. have a step and I think it is step number 2. This step says to “get out of the denial stage” which means that you quit lying to yourself. Lies are more damaging with time. They get worse. Remember that people always lie. Someone once said to "Believe half of what you see and NOTHING of what you hear". Just because you read it, or hear it, doesn’t make it true.

The next time you call someone a liar, or complain that they lie, remember it probably has not been very long since you lied. If this is not an area where you struggle, consider yourself fortunate.

23.title: Pornography
23.verse: God wants you to be holy and to stay away from sexual sins.
23.quote: All sins are attempts to fill voids.
23.wisdom:
I know it sounds like a strange subject for a dad to be writing to his daughter but it is a serious one. Pornography is a massive addiction in this country especially for men. It is degrading to women and just bad all the way around. Beware of men that you date and hang out with and their addiction to pornography. It really does eat at their brain and puts all sorts of bad images and expectations in their minds.

A guy that talks to you about pornography or mentions they have “seen something” you should try, is the wrong person to be around. This includes Playboy magazine, "Any"-rated movies, just about the entire internet, or anything of any kind that degrades women. Sadly there is a very short distance for the majority of men between the slippery slope of pornography that starts with the "barely bad" to the really sick. It is an addiction and just gets worse.

Pornography has no place in a relationship; married or otherwise. Stay away from it, and stay away from men that find it fascinating.

24.title: Gossip
24.verse: And besides they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house, and not only idle but also gossips and busybodies, saying things which they ought not.
24.quote: No one gossips about other peoples secret virtues.
24.wisdom:
The reality is that I have experienced, and I’m sure you have too, the negative effect of gossip. It is really damaging to all parties involved. One of my buddies says there are three types of class of people (He didn’t mean money.)

Lowest class: Talks about other people

Middle class: Talks about themselves

Upper class: Talks about ideas and vision

People who gossip usually do so because they want and need someone to compare themselves to so they can feel better about themselves. Someone else’s misery in a weird way makes their problems not seem so bad.

This is one of many of the subjects that I tell you one thing and then invariably I may do something else. I don’t have a large problem with gossip because I usually don’t have much to gossip about with anyone. There are certainly times when I get some information and it is hard not to pass it on. Sadly, that is gossip. I am sure you are challenged as well.

Don’t be a gossip as an adult.

25.title: Memories
25.verse: I will forgive them for the wicked things they did And I will not remember their sins anymore.
25.quote: Not the power to remember, but it’s very opposite, the power to forget, is a necessary condition of our existence.
25.wisdom:
Your memory is not as good as you think it is. This is a tough lesson to learn but a reality of life that when learned makes it easier. I have found that I remember how bad the “bad” things were, yet I don’t always remember the good things. At the same time, the bad has a tendency to look worse in the rear view mirror and I have a hard time remembering the circumstances and all the other things that were a part of my memory.

There are so many things that I have forgotten over the years. Some forever, and some things I remember only after something or someone reminds me of it. I cherish the memories that I have because sometimes it is all I have of the past. Many people live their life with some sort of baggage that is related to a bad memory. They can’t remember the whole thing or they just remember parts of it. What they do remember can hold them hostage for life. This isn’t always a bad memory. Sometimes they are good ones that can hold us hostage. Some people "peak" in high school and never want to leave that period of their life. You know them: the football star, the girl that always had a boyfriend in high school when no one else did, guy with the coolest car.

Make sure as you move forward that you don’t rely on just your memory of things. Many things that happened to you as a child you remember through the eyes of a child. Sometimes that is good and sometimes it is bad. Use the other people around you to get a better perspective, or at least a different perspective, on the situation. Ask all the people around you what they thought of a situation. You know that everyone’s opinion will always be different.

That is the case if you just ask someone about something that happened last week! What it teaches you is that there is more that happened, and you don’t have that memory.

If you ask others, you can gain more perspective.

It will keep you out of bondage for both good and bad memories that can hold you back from being all God would want you to be.

26.title: Things I Remember
26.verse: You gave me life and showed me kindness And in your care you watched over my life.
26.quote: Life can only be understood backwards, But it must be lived forwards.
26.wisdom: You were a really great soccer player. I loved your voice and your laugh. You were a very loud kid! You are a great sister. One of my favorite things ever was to race you up the stairs for bed time. I can remember you studying for a school test in the shower with your papers wrapped in plastic!

27.title: New College Friends
27.verse: Some friends may ruin you but a real friend will be more loyal than a brother.
27.quote: The only reward of virtue is virtue; the only way to have a friend is to be one.
27.wisdom:
They are a reflection of who you are and what you do. We can’t live without friends and if we pick the wrong ones we may not live at all. Pick great friends in college and be a great friend to others. We have told you to seek out Christian friends.

Friends are with you through good and bad. Friends know you and accept you just the way you are. Friends are willing to correct you when necessary while always letting you understand that they love you just the same. College will give you the opportunity to add new friends. Pick very, very wisely. Friends will influence you. Make sure it is a good influence. You will meet a lot of people who have grown up in a different environment than you. Some better and some worse. Make sure that your friends are going to build you up and bring you joy, and that you do the same for them.

Everyone at one time or another in his or her life experiences a friend that is not good for them. You know it but you have let them get close to you and it becomes hard to let go. Don’t get sucked in by people who look like they have “experienced” more bad things than you and they are better off for it. They aren’t. If it was wrong and dangerous, they haven’t “lived more” than you; they just dodged a bullet and got away with it. Maybe they won’t next time and you won’t “dodge the bullet” the first time. Can you live with the consequences, and secondly, do you want to live with the consequences? Life is dangerous enough without courting new problems.

Let go of bad friends. Better yet, don’t start with them. You will be better off in the short and long run. I would love to get to know your new friends as you get older. That would have been somewhat weird when you were under 18. Now it is cool.

28.title: Abortion
28.verse: Before I made you in your mother’s womb, I chose you Before you were born, I set you apart for a special work I appointed you as a prophet to the nations.
28.quote: There is one thing alone That stands the brunt of life throughout its course; A quiet conscience.
28.wisdom:
I have met a number of women who have had abortions. You may actually know women yourself who have had abortions. The ones I have met live with a sorrow and pain that cannot be described. They “killed” their own flesh and blood. I also know people who had kids when they were 15 years old. Another had one when she was 17. They gave them up for adoption. While they regret getting in trouble early in life, they have no regrets that these kids are alive today. No burden, no damage just the knowledge that because they made a mistake they didn’t make two and end up living with the fact that someone else had to die because of their mistake.

This doesn’t mean that there aren’t people out there that say they weren’t impacted negatively by having an abortion. I don’t know any and quite frankly I can’t imagine how they were not negatively impacted over the course of their life.

Sometimes people justify it because the “man” wanted it to happen or didn’t want to have any responsibility. If that is the case, then don’t let them lead in this situation. A child’s life is far more important than their embarrassment, reputation, parents, etc.

Abortion is an easy short-term solution with hard long term consequences. Having a child and giving it up for adoption is a really hard short-term solution with really great long-term consequences. I am not telling you this just for you. I want you to save yourself for your husband (see other topic) but I also want you to give good advice if you are ever presented with the opportunity to help someone. In the unlikely situation that you ever end up in this situation yourself, I hope you would heed this advice as well.

29.title: The Bible
29.verse: All scripture is given by God and is useful for teaching, for showing people what is wrong in their lives, for correcting faults and for teaching how to live right.
29.quote: You can learn more about human nature by reading the Bible than by living in New York
29.wisdom:
It really is pretty sad that I have spent so much time dispensing advice to you and expecting that you will read it. The reality is that you will be far better off if you put this list down and just read the Bible. That goes for everything I say and everything that all the men and women of earth have said as well (including you!). We fall so short with our miniscule perspectives on things.

At 18, you have seen virtually nothing in this world, I have seen twice as much as you, and I know nothing as well.

Two people were talking and one person said there was no God. After arguing back and forth for a while one man took out a paper plate and said to the other, “Imagine that all of the world’s knowledge is represented by this paper plate. Everything that could ever be known in and about this world is on this plate. How much of this plate do you think represents what you know of this world? The guy took a pen and made a tiny dot on the plate. The questioner responded, “Don’t you think there just may be some information that you don’t know that might make you wrong?”

I appreciate you reading these and I know that you love me. That gives me an opportunity to share with you some of my life lessons. It’s all garbage compared to what God has to say. I hope that my advice just follows His. I know that intellectually you know that to be true. I just wanted to make sure that I said it and to make sure that you knew that I recognized it as well.

30.title: Anger
30.verse: Don’t get angry, Don’t be upset; it only leads to trouble
30.quote: Anger is never without an argument But seldom with a good one.
30.wisdom:
You have heard this a million times and you will probably hear it a million more times. Holding on to anger buys you nothing. Staying angry and holding grudges only hurts you far more than it does the other person or thing you are angry about. I repeat it just because if you don’t get this, it can control you and can control your life. Smart, intelligent, successful, bright, and creative people have been strangled by anger and grudges.

Here is an example: A divorced kid has been given the unfortunate opportunity to have things to be angry about or hold grudges. The reality is that they don't have any more things to be angry about than anyone else. Everyone has issues and things to be angry over; it is just that the divorced kid's anger is more “socially okay” to hold onto. Everyone can feel their pain and understand if they are angry with their mom, dad or espeically a stepparent, etc. Today’s society gives much more latitude for this.

Problems from childhood, and tough circumstances can be used as crutches and excuses. People near you, and even those who love you, will always “cut you some slack” for your past. Therapists and counselors drive BMW’s and Mercedes because of it. It is socially acceptable to be angry with an ex-spouse, parent or stepparent, etc., for a lifetime, if you choose. The problem is that social acceptance just makes it harder to get rid of it, and getting rid of it is the only survival plan you can have.

There are even people that use the “anger” and say that it helps drive them to be better or makes them focus more. In virtually every instance that is a load of crap. Maybe and rarely for a short short period. Over time it doesn’t help anyone under any circumstances, and there are far better ways to get motivated and live your life.

31.title: Treating your Mom with Respect
31.verse: A wise daughter makes her father happy But a foolish daughter disrespects her mother.
31.quote: An injury is much sooner forgotten than an insult.
31.wisdom:
If there is one area where I would like to see you continue and even improve as an adult, it would be treating your Mom with respect and honoring her. You need to treat everyone with respect including me. Your mom deserves, and has earned an extra measure of respect, as have all moms. (I think dads have as well, but I am the one writing this...) Obviously, it is one of the Ten Commandments.

A mother-child relationship is never perfect. It can’t be. You have two people separated by 20 some years with a passionate interest in the outcome of the “younger of the two”. Both believe they have earned the right and also are “right” about what to do. Honor your Mom with your words, thoughts and actions. She deserves it. Measure your words with her. She loves you and only wants the best for you. She isn’t perfect and I am not telling you to blindly respect each and every one of her actions or choices if you don’t. She would not want that either. I ask that you honor her and respect her because she is your mother. I also ask that you simply love her.

If you do that; the rest comes easy.

32.title: Favorite Color
32.verse: The Lord has glory and majesty He has power and beauty in His temple
32.quote: A thing of beauty is a joy forever
32.quote_attr: Its loveliness increases; it will never
32.wisdom:
Pass into nothingness John Keats

I used to think it was pretty stupid that Ditto had a favorite color. I was wrong. I never really had one. I like blue but it didn’t mean that much to me. I think it is impressive now to have a favorite color. Love your choice of yellow. I think it is cool to have a unique personality. I think it is cool to have things about you that are unique and special that help others to get to know you better and understand you.

It requires you to share these with people so they can get to know you, appreciate you and enjoy you. You are a little like me. We have a tendency to be a little on the “less expressive/less sharing” side when it comes to personal stuff. We can learn a lesson from those people who are comfortable sharing.

We may never be like them but if we move towards opening up it can only help people to know us, and enjoy us. I am convinced that the more people know about you the MORE they will like you.

33.title: Treating the things you own...
33.verse: Those who have understanding will be given more And they will have all they need. But those who do not Have understanding, even what they have will be taken from them
33.quote: Property has its duties as well as it’s rights
33.wisdom:
One of the signs of someone who is grateful and respectful of what they have been blessed with is how they take care of those things. Like everyone, I can do a much better job of this.

This means to take care of your car, clothes, house and body. I know your room isn’t perfect and mine isn’t either. Just remember that if you take care of things that you own, you will probably get an opportunity to own more things. In Christian speak this is called stewardship.

It might be money, job, responsibility, kids, etc. Be a great steward.

34.title: Cut Your Losses
34.verse: God knows who is evil and when he sees evil, he takes note of it.
34.quote: Tis strange what a man may do, and a woman yet think him an angel.
34.wisdom:
If he doesn’t treat you like you are the only woman in the world to him…Dump him. Don’t ever believe or think that somehow or another there is some man that is better than you or that he has the right to treat you like anything less than a queen (You have heard me use this term before...).

If you allow someone to treat you bad, they will lose respect for you, and worse, you will lose respect for yourself. Not everyone will treat you like a queen. That is okay; just don’t EVER go out with them again. There will be times when you will chase some guy because you think he is perfect, or just right. If you catch him and he doesn’t treat you right, recognize that he has bad taste and you made a mistake.

Fishermen call this term "catch and release". Just because you decide to chase him and maybe even catch him, does NOT mean that you should not throw him back.

35.title: Danger
35.verse: The Lord is like a strong tower Those who do right can run to him for safety
35.wisdom:
Shakespeare

The first place is always better than the second place...

I once heard a San Diego policeman tell us one time that if you are ever attacked by someone run immediately because the first place is always better than the second. This means that if they are going to hurt you in public they will do much worse things in private.

He gave examples of time and time again where people were talked into going to another place and ended up having more harm done to them. He even said if someone was standing five feet away from you with a gun, that you should run. 80% of the people shooting will miss and over 90% won't shoot at all in public. His point was if they are crazy enough to shoot you in public, they would do much worse in private. How do you do this? Use the following:

If someone gets in your car for example in a mall, crash it right away right in the parking lot. Don't drive somewhere else.

Throw your money away and run in the other direction. If they want your money you will be okay. If they didn't, you have a head start.

If you are in a restaurant and someone comes in to hold it up; get up and run out right then and there. Don't wait.

Have a plan of where and when you are going to run with friends. I know those sound crazy but he said it would save your life.

36.title: Consequences
36.verse: Remember this: The person who plants a little will have a small harvest, But the person who plants a lot will have a big harvest.
36.quote: You can do anything in this world if you’re prepared to take the consequences.
36.wisdom:
For everything we do on this earth, and for some things that are done to us, we have consequences. Sometimes the consequences are good and sometimes they are bad. We can be sure that we will have consequences. As an adult, the consequences seem to get more serious, and we are in a position to have the opportunity to create more consequences and impact others as well.

As a child you get scolded by your parents, and if you are really, really bad you may go to military school. As an adult, no one scolds you, but if you are really bad you go to prison.

As a child, if you get in a car accident your parents pay. As an adult, you pay and you may also get to go to prison.

As a child if you win the lottery, your parents have to collect. As an adult, you get to keep the money (minus 40% in taxes)

As a child, if I go to the wrong place I may be spanked or lost. As an adult, if I go to the wrong place I may be raped or murdered.

You get the point. You have watched your dad reap the consequences of my actions; good and bad. You have seen how they have affected you; good and bad. What is really important to remember is that you can’t always see and measure the consequences before the action you take. No matter how well thought out your actions may be you can never really measure all the consequences.

As you make decisions as an adult beware of the consequences good and bad. Take note of the impact your decisions will make.

37.title: Never Ever
37.verse: A fool always loses his temper, but a wise man holds it back.
37.quote: The worst tempered people I’ve ever met were the people who knew they were wrong.
37.wisdom:
There is no instance, under ANY circumstances, that a man should strike you in any form or fashion. Not “accidents,” alcohol, your miserable/awful behavior, you hit him (which you should never do!), you provoke him, drugs, his past/parents, his friends, job, bad day at work, money, kids...you get the point.

There are no conditions whatsoever. If it ever happens, it is NEVER your fault and you should run as fast as you can. Call the police/me/your mom/brother/grandparents, anyone who can help. If he hits you, he will keep hitting you and he will hit your kids. You can guarantee it.

One other comment for you. You can see signs of this based on his temper. The bible is pretty clear on not marrying or being connected to someone who has a temper. It is a bad thing and you should avoid it.

38.title: Travel
38.verse: For he looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under heaven.
38.quote: For my part, I travel not to go anywhere, but to go. I travel for travel’s sake. The great affair is to move.
38.wisdom:
Robert Louis Stevenson

Travel anywhere and everywhere that you can. Very few things can help you grow to adulthood and continue to grow after that better than traveling. The more different people that you meet and see in their environments the better you can be. There is nothing more powerful than to see how other people, countries, families live to help you understand your experience better.

Your "world" is much smaller than when I grew up. With the internet the world is a much smaller place. Reach out and connect, you will be a better person for it.

39.title: Working Hard
39.verse: A person who does not work hard Is just like someone who destroys things.
39.quote: It is better to wear out, than to rust out.
39.wisdom:
Hard work (effort) requires no intelligence, money, advantage or connections. It just requires commitment and perseverance. Your ability to work hard for school will be a great advantage to you in life. You already know a key secret to success in life; working hard on the important things in your life. Someday you can use this to work hard on your marriage, raising your kids, staying connected to friends, your relationship with Christ just to name a few.

You have talent and skills that when put to use with hard work and effort; you can do anything that you strive for. It all comes down to your priorities.

Make sure that in the coming years you put your effort and priority into your relationship with Christ, your family, your health, your work/school and your friends. They are all important to you. When kept in this priority you will excel.

40.title: Embarrassment
40.verse: For you are my hope; O Lord God, you are my confidence from my youth.
40.quote: If you're never scared or embarrassed or hurt, it means you never take any chances.
40.wisdom:
Almost as destructive as fear, anger or arrogance is embarrassment controlling your life. Embarrassment is an area that I have always struggled with that has been damaging to me. I can’t tell you not to be embarrassed because that it almost impossible. Just don’t let it control you. I can remember many instances where I missed out on doing things because I was embarrassed, or thought I would be embarrassed.

An example would be not asking a girl out because I was afraid to be embarrassed if she said no. It is kind of weird. I was not afraid of rejection but the embarrassment of people knowing I was rejected. Pretty sad, huh!

You know people that do not get embarrassed about anything. Maybe in some areas from your perspective or mine they should be. But should they? They don’t let what other people think affect what you they say, their friends, what they wear, what they like, etc. Seems like a lot less baggage for them than many people carry. The vast majority of feelings of embarrassment are false.

There are so many amazing things you will do and experience in life. Don’t be held back because you fear embarrassment. It is not worth what you will miss.

41.title: Sex and Guys
41.verse: Let us live in the right way, like people who belong to the day. We should not have wild parties and get drunk. There should be no sexual sin of any kind, no fighting or jealousy.
41.quote: There is nothing like desire for preventing the thing one says from bearing any resemblance to what one has in one’s mind.
41.wisdom:
Romans 13:13

There is nothing like desire for preventing the thing one says from bearing any resemblance to what one has in one’s mind.

Marcel Proust

The standard line is that “Guys are only after ONE thing.” They want sex and they will do anything to get you into bed. The sad thing is that for many guys that is the truth. My guess is that it doesn’t matter if they are a Christian or not. If this is their focus and direction nothing will stop them except for you. You can always stop them.

Some food for thought:

Sex is not the NEXT step to a more mature relationship. It is not a step but a benefit of marriage. If you don’t see it as a “step” to get closer or the next “stage” of a relationship then it won’t be an option. Anyone that tells you that it is necessary, natural, or required, is lying to you. Sex fogs everything. The desire for sex is just as foggy as actual sex in a relationship. Once it occurs, you can’t think straight.

Nice looking, parent friendly, sweet and caring guys will still lie about the need and necessity to have sex.

You and your sexual purity is the one precious thing you can give to your husband.

You don’t need “experience” with sex before marriage. There is no upside to being experienced with sex prior to marriage.

You are not missing anything by not playing the field. All you may do is feel bad later and have to carry the burden of other experience(s) if you have sex before marriage.

You will have a stronger marriage if you wait.

42.title: Fear
42.verse: The Lord is my light and the one who saves me. I fear no one. The Lord protects my life I am afraid of no one.
42.quote: Let me assert my firm belief that the only thing we have to fear is fear itself.
42.wisdom:
This is one word that will imprison you if don’t fight it all the time. Be aware of when you are afraid, and as you have heard me say before: “Face your fears.” I am sure that you know people that immediately come to mind when you think of fearful people.

Fear can wreck your life. People fear flying and never travel. People fear trusting people and never have loving relationships. People fear "not having a job" and stay in dead end positions and companies for the rest of their lives.

Don’t let that happen to you. I am sure you are saying that you are not afraid to travel, etc. That is not the point. Don’t let any fear hold you back. Recognize it and see it for what it is. Don’t let fear control your life.

There is one thing to fear and that is God. The bible says, “Wisdom is the Fear of God.” That is a fear you can have.

43.title: Jesus is Lord and Savior
43.verse: Jesus answered: I am the truth, the way, and the life No one comes to the Father except through me.
43.quote: ...that people often say about Him: "I'm ready to accept Jesus as a great moral teacher, but I don't accept His claim to be God." That is the one thing we must not say. A man who was merely a man and said the sort of things Jesus said would not be a great moral teacher. He would either be a lunatic--on a level with the man who says he is a poached egg--or else he would be the Devil of Hell. You must make your choice. Either this man was, and is, the Son of God: or else a madman or something worse. You can shut Him up for a fool, you can spit at Him and kill Him as a demon; or you can fall at His feet and call Him Lord and God. But let us not come with any patronizing nonsense about His being a great human teacher. He has not left that open to us. He did not intend to.
43.wisdom:
The savior part is when you make a decision for Christ. You submit to His will. That is how you get to heaven.

The Lord part is much tougher. That is when you try to live your life to please Him. You do that because you recognize that it is by His sheer grace that you have the many blessings you have today. Your looks, brains, home, family, the fact that you live in the United States, etc. is all by the grace of God. You did nothing to get these; they were given to you. Lordship with Christ means that you recognize the following:

He is bigger than any problem or solution that you may have. Let me say that again: He is bigger than any problem or solution that you may have. Without centering your life on His standards, yours will move. Live by His standards. You do this to please Him. Since He designed everything you can feel confident knowing that "you" are working as designed!

44.title: Work to Live
44.verse: People can work hard using all their wisdom, knowledge and skill but they will die, and The other people will get the things for which they worked. They did not do The work, but they will get everything. This is also unfair and useless.
44.quote: Perpetual devotion to what a man calls his business is only to be sustained by perpetual neglect of many other things.
44.wisdom:
Work to live don't live to work.

Simple concept. Figure it out early and you will be better for it. Make sure this is the way you live, your future spouse lives, and that you teach this to your kids. I have met WAY too many workaholic successful men and women. They are successful but deep down they regret the time they have spent at work. Don't be like that.

45.title: Love Language
45.verse: It is better to correct someone openly Than to have love and not show it.
45.quote: Love conquers all things; let us too surrender to love.
45.wisdom:
WORDS

Tell people, show people and remind people that you love them. For the people you love, tell them. This includes your future husband as well as your family. For example, make sure you tell everyone in your family that you love them. Tell your mom you love her; all the time.

Show the people you love that you love them. Everyone responds to a different love language. Harville Hendricks says there are five love languages. They are:

Words of Affirmation: Saying nice things

Gifts: Receiving gifts

Quality time: Spending time with them

Acts of Service: Doing things for them

Physical touch: Hugs, kisses (someday sex with your husband)

Everyone has a different love language. Some have more than one. Find out what they are!

PS: You can tell me you love me too!.

46.title: Arrogance
46.verse: God can’t stomach arrogance or pretense; believe me, he’ll put those upstarts in their place.
46.quote: By my count, more business leaders have failed and derailed because of arrogance than any other character flaw.
46.wisdom:
There seems to be something about the world today that has fallen in love with arrogance. The more successful you are the more accepting it is to be arrogant. Some people say “they are not arrogant”, they are just confident. There is nothing wrong with confidence. We all need it.

The difference is when we begin to think that we are uniquely special. We begin to think we are better than other people. It usually happens in areas that we had no control over from the start. People are arrogant about where they live, the car they drive, how they look, their talents, how much money they have, etc. At your age, how many of these do you really have control over? I really dislike arrogant people. They just really bug me. Make sure you can see the difference between confidence and arrogance.

Be confident. You have many reasons to be confident. Enjoy that but don’t let it get out of hand and become arrogant.

47.title: My Thoughts
47.verse: A person who does not work hard Is just like someone who destroys things.
47.quote: It is better to wear out, than to rust out.
47.wisdom:
You are no longer a minor. We can go vote to together, buy a pack of cigarettes (just kidding!), join the army together, etc., etc.

Thank you for 18 years. You don’t remember them all but I do. The day you were born was very, very special. I had always dreamed and hoped that someday I would have a child. I had no idea what a miracle you would be. I couldn’t stop smiling, laughing, shouting and crying when you came. You don’t understand that but God willing someday you will get the opportunity to have a child.

I am ready to have a child that is an adult. I will always see you as my little girl. Please be patient with me as I learn to treat you and communicate with you as an adult (who will always be my little girl). I can’t wait to have an adult parent/child relationship with my adult daughter. It will and can be our best time together.

Let’s get started right now…

DO LIFE!

48.title: Pride
48.verse: First pride-then the crash; the bigger the ego the harder the fall
48.quote: A man's pride can be his downfall, and he needs to learn when to turn to others for support and guidance.
48.wisdom:
The dictionary definition of pride is: *a high or inordinate opinion of one's own dignity, importance,merit, or superiority, whether as cherished in the mind or as displayed in bearing, conduct, etc.*

Nobody wants to be prideful yet everyone struggles with it. Pride is all self-driven destruction. No outside assistance or contribution. Just each one of us getting a warped perspective of ourselves in some area of our life. We begin to think our "pooh does not stink". The result is lost jobs, friendships, opportunity, marriages, accidents,etc., etc. It sneaks up on you and causes havoc. The bible says God hates pride. I can see why.

The other interesting thing about pride is that it is ugly. Very unattractive. Watch out! Beware! Caution!

I do not want this to be a complete downer...

There is an idiom (*a group of words established by usage as having a meaning not deducible from those of the individual words*) called:

*Pride and joy*- someone or something cherished, valued, or enjoyed above all others.

THIS WOULD BE YOU.

49.title: Manipulation
49.verse: ...know for sure that you will be punished for your sin.
49.quote: All sin tends to be addictive, and the terminal point of addiction is what is called damnation
49.wisdom:
I know that is a pretty tough bible verse and quote, but this is an area that I really do think you and "everyone else" needs to watch out for. That area is manipulation.

Unfortunately you are very good at it. Sadly, so is everyone else, me included. "We" have learned (I am assuming this is a learned trait.) over many, many years and probably many successful outcomes to manipulate to get our way. Either you do not tell the whole story, add additional items, gauge when and where you communicate information, all with a goal to get your way, keep getting your way or avoid something you do not want. The reason it is so dangerous is that you are good at it and in many instances it works for you.

As you know, the problem is that it creates massive distrust with those whom you love and those that love you. People feel used and misled. The bigger issue is a loss of trust. Trust is something that you earn each and every day. It is like a bank account that you add to or subtract from. As a child, the consequence for manipulation has been loss of “stuff” like phones, computers, sleepovers and car time. All small things in the world of life all handed down by people (your Mom and Dad) who love you unconditionally no matter what you do or how you act.

In an adult world the consequences will be much worse such as loss of job and loss of relationships, and people that you hold dear. . Maybe even more important is that now as an adult you are building a reputation and a witness for all the world to see.

Make it a goal to be bad at manipulation. Quit practicing and get worse at this. The sooner the better.

50.title: New Rules
50.verse: She is strong and respected by the people She looks forward to the future with joy.
50.quote: I have seen the future and it works.
50.wisdom:
Welcome to Being an Adult. This is you are a not a kid anymore lingo. We love you and always want you around but now that you are 18; you have more choices. Note: Just because you have the choice does not necessarily make it a good one...

CHRISTINE 18TH BIRTHDAY CHANGES

Old requirements No vegetable requirements No chores No vacation or holiday requirements

You are always welcome at our house. (Now that you are 18; you are "free" if you want to be.) Anytime. For a day, week, month, years… When we take a vacation, you are always welcome to join us for the vacation we are on. Note: We will always pay for the entire vacation if you take the entire vacation with us. I will always include you in the planning so you can make the vacation with us if you want.

New Requirements

If you come to visit/live, come because you want to be with us and don’t be angry about it. Examples of ways you show us you want to be with us: Eat some meals with us, talk with us, buys us dinner/lunch etc., go to the store or Starbucks with us, watch TV or a movie with us, etc.

You have no chores but come with an attitude to want to participate and help out. If when you come you only take, take, take and never give, you will wear out your welcome.

If you are staying with us and we go to church, we expect you to join with us. If you stay with us, you will have a curfew that will go to 12:00pm unless rarely delayed for some unique reason.

More financial details to follow.

51.title: Being An Adult
51.verse: Don’t stop listening to correction my child, Or you will forget what you have already learned.
51.quote: The future...something which everyone reaches at The rate of sixty minutes and hour, whatever he does, whoever he is.
51.wisdom:
CONGRATULATIONS! You are now once again the youngest as in the youngest adult there can be at 18 years of age. Just when you had made it to the top, you are right back at the beginning again. I am so very proud of you. 18 years of age and you have your entire life ahead of you to LIVE.

Live it well and live it as it should be because it is the only one you will ever have on this Earth. One of the ways you prepare for eternity is by living a full life here. I hope that one or two of the things I had to tell you will be of value to you now that you are 18. Take the very best and worst of all those around you, mix it in with the very best and worst of yourself these past 18 years and match it up against the Bible for a truth test and GO FOR IT.

You have such flexibility and such wide opportunity ahead. You can do so much. I saw a license plate the other day that said: If you are living as if there is not a God…you had better be right. That is true but it should read just the opposite. If you are living as if there is a God; you are right and ENJOY all that He has given you. You really have been given quite a bit in your first 18 years. You are blessed; you really are. You have so much still ahead of you. Don’t be afraid to make a mistake. Don’t be fearful. You are loved, cherished, prayed for, appreciated, approved of, accepted just the way you are.

My love for you is unconditional. It always has been and always will be. You already have done enough for me to love you with all my heart just by being born. You are precious, unique, special, loved, appreciated, significant, valuable, cherished and wanted. I am so very impressed with you. You have such talent, beauty, creativity, humor, confidence and intelligence. I have said this before…You are perfectly imperfect.

The problem is that it now means that I have a daughter that is 18 years of age and I think I am too young to have a daughter that old. You have given me an unbelievable 18 years. They have not all been perfect but at the same time, I feel incredibly proud to be your Dad.

52.title: Praying
52.verse: Lord hear my prayer; listen to my cry for mercy. Answer me because you are loyal and good.
52.quote: One single grateful thought raised to heaven is the most perfect prayer.
52.wisdom:
There is really one subject left that I need to share with you. It isn’t the 52nd most important one; it is just the last one. I wanted to share with you how important it is for you to pray for everything that you do. I really believe that we all need “prayer cover.” This means that we need people praying for us, and we need to be praying for others and ourselves.

Since the day I became a Christian, I have prayed for you unceasingly. It makes a difference and I want to encourage you to bring your challenges, hopes and dreams to God. Life is exciting and wonderful, but it is also very hard. You can’t do it on your own, and you shouldn’t try. Recognize your position, and recognize that it is by the grace of God we exist and breathe. It is easy to ask because He is worth asking.

I have enjoyed sharing these ideas with you. I also enjoy praying for you. I request that you pray for me as well. I need it. It is more important than sending me a birthday card or calling me on Father’s Day.

Thank you for the past 18 years. God willing we will have many, many more years together.

1.title: Don't Compare Yourself to Others
1.verse: A sound heart is life to the body But envy is rottenness to the bones
1.quote: The truest mark of being born with great qualities is being born without envy.
1.wisdom:
You would figure that the “competition, comparisons, measuring up, cliques, groups, etc.” would be gone once you leave high school and turn 18. You would think social pressures and people wondering about what everyone else thinks and does would go away.

It doesn’t.

I have seen far too many people well into adult life that are still comparing themselves to everyone else. They are still trying to keep up with the rich neighbor, thin relative, famous schoolmate, or popular fellow worker. It is a waste of time and not worth the effort. You can’t win, but you can lose.

High school, especially senior year, is rampant with people comparing where they are, where they are headed next year, and what they have accomplished. There is always someone who did better than we did and people whom did worse. The problem is that not everyone started in the same place and we know for a fact that high school is NOT the finish line. We have each been given things we can control and things we can’t. You can’t control the fact that you are bright, smart, handsome (your dad is allowed to say that!), and funny anymore than you can control the house or the country where you were born. You can control how you react to conflict, hardship, success, and commitment to God, family, friends and enemies.

Expect the best from yourself no matter what your circumstances. Don’t compare your success or failure to others. Measure your "place" to your own dreams/goals and what God wants for your life.

2.title: Seeking Advice from Others
2.verse: "Every word of God is flawless; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
2.quote: Successful people follow the same advice they prescribe for others.
2.wisdom:
They say in business that free advice isn’t worth anything. I disagree. Seeking advice to help you make decisions is critical to your success as an adult and a teenager. Finding people who have experience that you can use to make decisions about your life is really valuable. That advice can steer you in the right direction and help you to live the life you were meant to live. The formula I use is simple: measure all advice in three ways:

First, does it match up to the Bible? It is the one place I can trust. Then I pray about it. Why not get the answer straight from the top? What is cool is that even people who aren’t Christians or Jews live by the truth that is in the Bible. Most don’t even know they are following it.

Second, does this person I am seeking advice have my best interest in mind? (Note: I first seek advice from people who are close to God. Whenever I am seeking real advice, I always see what their relationship is like with God at that time. Usually I will ask, “How is your walk these days? From there I can measure the advice.) Do they like me and care for me? People who love you are a great place to get input. Despite my shortcomings at times that is why you should always ask me for advice whether you use it or not.

Third, does this person have a personal interest in the question? If so, then I might have to be very careful with their advice. This is especially true in relationships. Seeking dating advice or listening to a buddy for example who likes the same girl you do would be a bad place to get advice

I am your biggest fan and will ALWAYS give you an answer that is in your best interest, even if you don’t like it.

3.title: Forgiveness
3.verse: For if you forgive men when they sin against you, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
3.quote: The weak can never forgive. Forgiveness is the attribute of the strong. — Anger makes you smaller, while forgiveness forces you to grow beyond what you were.
3.wisdom:
There is probably no stronger attribute that a person can have than the ability to forgive and ask for forgiveness. In many instances it is just a very small action on your part and a huge impact on the people you love and even those you don't. The inability to forgive is much harder on you than it will ever be on the other person. The reason is that when you don't forgive, you give up control of your peace, joy, and, sometimes, sanity to either the other person or the action that occurred. That is too hard and way too much to give away.

The most challenging forgiveness for me is forgiving myself. How about you? I do really well when it comes to other people. It is almost easy for me to see the best in other people. When you see the best in others, their challenges, and their problems, then the things they do to you are much easier to forgive. It doesn't always work for me. What is crazy is that Christ died on the cross so we can be forgiven. If we don't forgive others, including ourselves, then what He did was a waste of time. Even with all that knowledge and comfort, I still struggle with that area.

How are you at forgiving others? Are there things and people you need to forgive? What about yourself? Do you need to ask forgiveness? Are you clean there as well? I hope so. I love you too much to have you burdened when the ability to forgive and be forgiven is right there in front of you. <mark>Just to make sure you are reading these, if you say the word forgiveness and give me a high five, I will give you ten dollars.</mark>

4.title: Sometimes No Advice is Better
4.verse: I can do all things through Christ, who gives me strength.
4.quote: I know God will not give me anything I can't handle. I just wish that He didn't trust me so much.
4.wisdom:
When you are right in the middle of God's will, you know it by the Bible, by prayer, and by those around you who are Godly and have wisdom. Stay there and keep your path.

Don't listen to anyone else, **including me**.

5.title: A Man She can Respect
5.verse: He was full of loving kindness, and we have all received so much kindness from him.
5.quote: This above all: to thine own self be true, And it must follow, as the night the day, Thou canst not then be false to any man.
5.wisdom:
Wow! You are <mark>18</mark> and I still fall way short in telling you all the things you need to know about women. Quite frankly, I have not done a very good job. First, because it always seems much more uncomfortable than it really is and second probably more important, I am not very sure how much I know. Here is my best shot:

I read a great book called “Love and Respect”. It says that women desire to be loved and men want to be respected. My first advice to you is that in order to be respected by a woman you need to be a man who deserves respect. Respect is something you earn from others by your actions to them and to everyone else. Being a man that a woman can respect is the one of the first steps to understanding how to have a great relationship.

A man of respect is someone who: fears God, treats others with respect, pulls their own weight, serves others, willing to fight for the less advantaged, giving, honest, above reproach in all they do, treats Mom with kindness and love; to just name a few.

Being a man a woman respects means that you do the following: Care for her, treat her like a queen, protect her, look out for her, serve her and encourage her. In a marriage that also means providing for her and your kids. In a boyfriend/girlfriend relationship it means treating her kindly, opening the door for her, buying her gifts, talking nicely to her (usually a lot of talking), speaking highly of her to your friends, treating her family with respect.

Yes, it is a lot of work but it is worth it.

6.title: Character
6.verse: Give him credit for all he does. He deserves the respect of everyone.
6.quote: Be more concerned with your character than your reputation, because your character is what you really are; your reputation is merely what others think you are.
6.quote_attr: John Wooden - Hall of Fame Basketball Coach
6.wisdom:
